sections.html:
Lawton is the Comanche County seat, in southwestern Oklahoma about 87 miles southwest of Oklahoma City. With 90,381 residents in the 2020 census it ranks as the sixth-largest city in the state and the biggest in the west. The Wichita Mountains rise just north of town, and Interstate 44 (the H. E. Bailey Turnpike here) runs through along with U.S. 62, 277 and 281.

The county assessor's office is at 315 SW 5th Street, Room 301, phone 580-355-1052. That office comes up repeatedly below, because values, homestead filings and protests all start there.

Fort Sill is the city's largest employer and puts nearly $2 billion a year into the region. Soldiers cycle through for training courses and unit moves, so some Lawton owners end up selling on a deadline set by orders, or after a rental tenant moved out and left repairs behind.

The base also affects individual homes. Aircraft noise from Henry Post Army Airfield reaches the northern part of Lawton, range noise carries beyond the post, and heavy artillery vibration is felt along the north-northeastern edge. If your house is in one of those areas, expect buyers to ask. Answer plainly and let them listen for themselves during a showing.

Lawton lies in Tornado Alley and sees about 31 days a year at or above 100 degrees. Long stretches of triple-digit heat wear on shingles, siding and air conditioners, and hail or wind season adds claims. Expect questions about roof age and past insurance claims, and keep the invoices and claim letters in a single folder.

sections.h2: Weeds, bulk waste and city bills
sections.html:
Grass or weeds taller than 12 inches break the Lawton code, and a property left that way can draw a court citation. The City Council also passed Ordinance 24-1810 in 2024 covering vacant lots, so anyone closing on or abandoning a lot should read it first.

When the city mows or hauls off bulk waste itself, an itemized bill follows. Fines run up to $300 for a first violation, $500 for a second within a year and $750 after that.

  • Cut the grass and clear debris ahead of each showing.
  • Follow the city's Solid Waste guidelines for bulk items.
  • Open any city bill the day it arrives, since the appeal clock starts on receipt.
  • Look up the Lawton Code of Ordinances on Municode for the section that fits your address.

Near downtown, the Downtown I Urban Renewal Plan calls for code enforcement to keep existing property from sliding into blight, so a neglected house there gets extra attention.

Tax bills are issued each year with a November 1 due date, and the county treasurer collects for the schools, city, county and other districts. Oklahoma lets an owner split the payment: half before January 1 and the rest before April 1. If the first half is missed, the entire balance goes delinquent.

The assessor lists and maintains records on every taxable parcel, helps with homestead filings, handles valuation protests and appears before the County Board of Equalization. Homestead applications are generally due by March 15, so confirm the date with the office before you file.

When the house sells, the title company usually checks the treasurer's balance. A spring closing with the second half still unpaid means that amount is divided at the table or paid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What to do first as a Lawton seller
sections.html:
Ask yourself what you need most: speed or the highest possible price. Putting the house on the market can attract a buyer with a loan, including military families, though you take on showings, inspection demands and the bank's calendar. Selling to us for cash is the quicker path for a place that needs repairs, has renters inside or is part of an estate.

Oklahoma requires the seller to give the buyer a disclaimer or a disclosure statement before an offer is accepted (60 O.S. section 833). Pull together permits, repair receipts and tax statements, then call us about the Lawton address. We walk through what a cash offer covers, and the decision stays with you.

sections.h2: Selling after a tenant or a move out
sections.html:
Plenty of Lawton houses sit empty after a lease ends or after a family is reassigned elsewhere. Vacant houses collect overgrown grass fast, and the 12-inch rule above applies whether anyone lives there or not. Arrange for someone to mow and check on the property, and keep the water and power connected so a buyer or inspector can see the house in daylight.

If there are belongings, damage or deferred repairs, say so when you call. We price those in instead of asking you to clean out and fix everything first, so you are not paying a hauler and a contractor before you learn what the house would bring.

sections.h2: Tax questions to settle before closing
sections.html:
Ring the Comanche County Treasurer to find out the balance and whether the second installment is still open. If the house has a homestead filing, ask the assessor's office whether the new owner must file again. A valuation you dispute goes to the assessor first and then to the County Board of Equalization, so raise it before you settle on a price.

Have the numbers in hand before you accept any offer, whether it is a listing buyer's or ours. A clear figure for taxes and any loan payoff tells you what you will actually take home.

After the first call, we ask about the house: what shape it is in, who occupies it, and whether a mortgage, lien or unpaid tax is attached. An offer follows in writing. Put it beside the likely net from a listing once repairs, agent fees and carrying months are subtracted, and take your time.

If you agree, a title company searches ownership and liens and prepares the papers. You can choose a closing date that fits a move or an orders window. At the table you sign, the title company pays any loan or tax balance out of the proceeds, and you get what remains. The house goes as it is. There are no buyer repair requests and no lender approval to wait for.

Bring a photo ID, the lender's name if you have a mortgage, your latest tax statement and any permit or repair receipts. If a tenant is still in the house, tell us at the start so the plan accounts for it.

faqs.a: Lawton had 90,381 residents in the 2020 census, making it the sixth-largest city in Oklahoma and the largest in the western part of the state.

faqs.q: Does Fort Sill noise affect Lawton house sales?
faqs.a: It can. Aircraft noise reaches the northern part of Lawton, and range noise carries off the base in every direction. Answer buyer questions honestly.

faqs.q: What is the weed height rule in Lawton?
faqs.a: Weeds or grass above 12 inches violate the city code, and the city can issue a court citation. Mowing costs the city bills to you can become a lien if unpaid after 30 days.

faqs.q: Who values property in Comanche County?
faqs.a: The Comanche County Assessor, at 315 SW 5th Street, Room 301 in Lawton, 580-355-1052. The Treasurer collects the tax, and valuation disputes go to the Assessor and then the County Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems when selling a house in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: Yes. Before the buyer's offer is accepted, you must deliver either a disclaimer statement or a condition disclosure statement, under 60 O.S. section 833.
